name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: it runs the edge routines edge_search, edge_seq, edge_close and edge_sync, then sweep(FN_SEARCH/FN_SEQ/FN_CLOSE/FN_SYNC, seed, 50000) for four fixed seeds; these update the static counters g_cases and g_fails through check(). It then prints a header and, for each function index 0..NFN-1, a row with FNNAME[i], g_cases[i] and g_fails[i], and returns 1 if any g_fails[i] is non-zero, otherwise 0. The function does write globals (indirectly, through the sweeps and edge routines); it does not write them in the printing loop.
note: slice shows the tail of main (harness.cpp:1005-1026). Reviewer round 15 is right: the old prose said no global is modified and that the sweeps had already run, but main itself calls the sweeps (lines 1007-1015).

name: ref___hdtoa
prose: Precondition: d is any double; xdigs points to the hex digit string; decpt, sign are valid int pointers; rve may be NULL; ndigits is the requested digit count (0 is treated as 1, negative means as many as needed). Postcondition: sets *sign from the sign bit of d. For zero it sets *decpt = 1 and returns nrv_alloc("0", rve, 1); for infinity it sets *decpt = INT_MAX and returns nrv_alloc("Infinity", rve, 8); for NaN or any unrecognised class it sets *decpt = INT_MAX and returns nrv_alloc("NaN", rve, 3). For normal and subnormal values (subnormals are scaled by 2^514 first) it sets *decpt from the exponent, allocates bufsize = ndigits (or SIGFIGS if ndigits < 0) with rv_alloc, rounds to ndigits hex digits when 0 < ndigits < SIGFIGS (this can change *decpt), writes a leading '1' followed by hex digits taken from the mantissa, trims trailing zero digits when ndigits was negative, NUL-terminates the string at position ndigits, sets *rve to that terminator if rve is not NULL, and returns the allocated string (to be released with freedtoa by the caller).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref___hdtoa (oracle.c:210-283); the dropped item was its tail. Returns checked at 228, 235, 238, 282.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: calls syslog_reset() and libsys_mock_reset(), runs the dirname, interposing-slot, arc4_stir and arc4_addrandom edge and random test routines, prints a header, one row per function (name, ncases[f], nfails[f]) and a TOTAL row, then returns 1 if the sum of nfails is non-zero and 0 otherwise. It modifies the global mock and counter state through the tests it runs.
note: slice shows the tail of main (harness.cpp:744-777). Contract removed: main touches global state.

name: ref_rangematch
prose: Precondition: pattern points just past the opening '[' of a NUL-terminated pattern (this function itself consumes a leading '!' or '^' as negation); test is the wide character to match; string is the position in the subject string after test; patmbs and strmbs point to mbstate_t objects; newp and news are writable pointers. Postcondition: returns RANGE_MATCH (1) when the bracket expression matches test (taking negation into account), RANGE_NOMATCH (0) when it does not match, or when the pattern contains a '/' while FNM_PATHNAME is set, or when mbrtowc finds an invalid or incomplete sequence in the pattern; and RANGE_ERROR (-1) for a malformed expression (pattern ends before the closing ']', a [. [= [: construct without its terminator, a collating symbol that is empty, unknown or multi-character where it is not allowed, a range start or end that is an equivalence class or character class, an unknown character class name, or a range end that is NUL). Only on the normal exit (after scanning to the closing ']') it stores a pointer just past that ']' in *newp and the current subject position in *news; this subject position can be ahead of the argument if a multi-character collating symbol or equivalence class consumed subject characters. Every early return leaves *newp and *news unmodified. *patmbs and *strmbs may be modified by the multibyte conversions.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_rangematch (oracle.c:896-1151). Old prose said *news receives the original string pointer, but lines 996, 1027 and 1148 show it may have advanced.

name: STUB_FUNCn-generated dispatchers (e.g. pthread_mutex_lock, pthread_cond_wait)
prose: Aggregate item that covers the STUB_FUNC, STUB_FUNC1, STUB_FUNC2 and STUB_FUNC3 macro definitions and about 60 invocations; it names no single function.
note: not one function: the macros (oracle.c:1298-1373) only forward to a function pointer in __thr_jtable[idx][0] or [1] and return its result; per-invocation entries would be needed to describe individual generated functions.

name: ref_fts_build
prose: Precondition: sp is a valid FTS handle, sp->fts_cur (cur) is a directory node, and type is BREAD, BNAMES or BCHILD. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (1) If __opendir2(cur->fts_accpath) fails it returns NULL; only when type == BREAD it also sets cur->fts_info = FTS_DNR and cur->fts_errno = errno; no directory stream was opened. Otherwise it reads all entries: when a chdir into the directory is needed (nlinks non-zero or type == BREAD) and fails, it sets FTS_DONTCHDIR on cur (and cur->fts_errno = errno when nlinks and type == BREAD) and every entry becomes FTS_NS with fts_errno = that errno if nlinks is non-zero or FTS_NSOK otherwise; entries that need no stat are FTS_NSOK, the others get their fts_info from fts_stat; afterwards, if FTS_NOSTAT_TYPE is set, any FTS_NSOK entry (including those from the failed-chdir case) is converted from d_type to FTS_DEFAULT, FTS_F, FTS_SL or FTS_W when d_type is one of the listed types. (2) If fts_alloc or growing the path buffer fails, it frees the entries so far, closes the stream, sets cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR, sets FTS_STOP, restores errno and returns NULL without changing the working directory back. (3) A readdir error sets cur->fts_errno and cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR if some items were read or FTS_DNR if not; the stream is closed. (4) If we descended and (type == BCHILD or no items were read) and changing back (to sp->fts_rfd at the root level, otherwise to ".." via the parent) fails, it frees the list, sets cur->fts_info = FTS_ERR, sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL. (5) If no items were found it returns NULL, and for type == BREAD sets cur->fts_info = FTS_DP unless it is already FTS_DNR or FTS_ERR. (6) Otherwise it sorts the list with fts_compar when there is one and more than one item and returns the head of the new singly linked list (owned by the caller). When FTS_NOCHDIR is set the path buffer is reset to its original length before exits (3) to (6).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_fts_build (oracle.c:742-1030). Reviewer round 15 is right (FTS_NOSTAT_TYPE conversion also applies to FTS_NSOK entries from the failed chdir). Old prose claimed the stream is 'always closed' and missed the FTS_DP case; both fixed.

name: ref_ftw
prose: Precondition: path is a NUL-terminated string and fn is a callable function pointer; no precondition on nfds (values below 1 are handled). Postcondition: if nfds < 1 it sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1 without doing anything else. Otherwise it opens an fts handle (FTS_LOGICAL | FTS_COMFOLLOW | FTS_NOCHDIR) on path and returns -1 with errno from fts_open if that fails. It then loops over fts_read: post-order directory visits (FTS_DP) are skipped; other entries are mapped to FTW_D, FTW_DNR, FTW_F, FTW_NS or FTW_SL and fn(path, stat, flag) is called; if fn returns a non-zero value the loop stops and that exact value is the result; a directory cycle (FTS_DC) sets errno = ELOOP and any other unexpected fts_info stops the loop, both giving result -1. When fts_read returns NULL (end of walk, or an error that this function does not check) the loop ends with result 0. After the loop it saves errno, calls fts_close, and if fts_close fails while the result is still 0 the result becomes -1 and errno is left as fts_close set it; otherwise errno is restored to its saved value. It returns the result.
note: checked oracle.c:29-88. Reviewer round 15 is right (precondition nfds >= 1 contradicted the EINVAL return); round 2 right (fts_read error not distinguished from end); round 1 right (callback value returned verbatim).

name: ref__citrus_db_hash_std
prose: Precondition: r points to a valid struct _region whose head is readable for _region_size(r) bytes. Postcondition: returns a uint32_t hash computed over the region bytes: starting from 0, for each byte it shifts hash left by 4, adds the ASCII-lowercased byte (only 'A'..'Z' are changed), and if any of the top four bits (mask 0xF0000000) are set, clears them in hash and XORs hash with them shifted right by 24. The region is not modified.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref__citrus_db_hash_std (oracle.c:549-570). Old prose said 'folding the high nibble into the low bits' which is vague; now exact.

name: ref_mbrtoc32_l
prose: Precondition: pc may be NULL; s may be NULL; if s is not NULL it points to at least n readable bytes; ps is NULL (the locale's own state is used) or points to an mbstate_t used as a conversion state; locale is valid or NULL (FIX_LOCALE substitutes the default). Postcondition: if s is NULL, or the state is not initialised, the function opens the iconv converter from the locale's codeset to UTF-32-INTERNAL; if that fails it marks the state uninitialised, sets errno = EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1; otherwise it clears the buffered source and destination lengths and marks the state initialised, and if s is NULL it returns 0 without writing *pc. With s non-NULL: if a converted character is already pending in the state it is delivered, written to *pc when pc is non-NULL, and the function returns (size_t)-3 (or 0 if that character is NUL), consuming no input. Otherwise at most MB_LEN_MAX minus the already buffered bytes of s are appended to the state's source buffer and conversion is attempted. If a character is produced it is stored in *pc when pc is non-NULL, the buffered source length is reset to 0, and the function returns the number of bytes of this call's input used (at least 1), or 0 if the character is NUL. If the converter reports an invalid sequence it discards the buffered input, sets errno = EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. If the input is an incomplete sequence it keeps the unconverted remaining bytes (srcleft of them) in the state's buffer and returns (size_t)-2. *pc is not written on the s == NULL, -1 and -2 paths.
note: checked oracle.c:785-866. Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 (s == NULL path, EINVAL) were right about older wording; round 15 is right (the -2 path keeps the unconsumed bytes, not 'all consumed').

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: calls edge_pass() and random_pass(), which fill the global counters ncase[] and nfail[]; prints a header and then, for each function f in 0..F_COUNT-1, a row with fname[f], ncase[f], nfail[f] and PASS or FAIL, followed by a TOTAL row with the sums; returns 0 if the total failure count is zero and 1 otherwise.
note: slice shows the tail of main (harness.cpp:498-523). Contract removed because main drives global state.

name: mock_mbrtowc
prose: Precondition: ps points to a _UTF8State holding the partial-character state (want, lbound, ch); pwc may be NULL; s may be NULL; otherwise s has at least n readable bytes. Postcondition: if us->want is outside 0..6 it sets errno = EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1 first of all. If s is NULL it behaves as if s were an empty string with n == 1 and pwc == NULL. If n == 0 it returns (size_t)-2 with no state change. With no pending partial character (want == 0): an ASCII byte is stored in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL and the function returns 1 (0 for NUL); a UTF-8 lead byte for 2 to 4 bytes starts decoding; any other lead byte sets errno = EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. When resuming (want != 0) it continues from the saved want, lbound and ch. A continuation byte that is not 10xxxxxx gives EILSEQ and (size_t)-1 with the state unchanged. If the input ends before the character is complete it saves the remaining count in us->want, lbound and ch and returns (size_t)-2 without writing *pwc. If complete but below lbound (overlong), a surrogate, or above U+10FFFF it sets EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1. Otherwise it stores the value in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL, sets us->want = 0 and returns the number of bytes consumed by this call (when resuming, the bytes that were still needed), or 0 if the decoded value is 0.
note: checked oracle.c:244-326. Reviewer round 15 first point is right (EINVAL return contradicts a precondition that want is 0..6). Its second point ('bytes consumed' wrong when resuming) is WRONG: on resume want = us->want is the remaining count (line 291) and the loop consumes exactly that many bytes, so the return value is the bytes consumed by this call.

name: ref_chainsearch
prose: Precondition: table is a valid struct xlocale_collate with valid info; key points to a readable NUL-terminated wide string; len points to a writable int; when info->chain_count > 0, chain_pri_table points to chain_count entries ordered the way the binary search expects (by first wide character, then by string). Postcondition: if chain_count <= 0 it returns NULL. Otherwise it binary-searches indices 0..chain_count-1: at each probe it compares *key with the entry's first wide character and, if equal, compares wcsncmp(key, entry->str, wcsnlen(entry->str, COLLATE_STR_LEN)); if that comparison is zero it stores the entry string length in *len and returns the entry; otherwise it moves low or high by the sign of the comparison. If no probe matches it returns NULL and *len is not modified. Because it stops at the first probe that matches, which of several matching chains is returned (for example a shorter prefix chain versus a longer one) depends on table order and the probe path. No other memory is modified.
note: checked oracle.c:218-247 (head present, defined through #define chainsearch ref_chainsearch at line 183). Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 are right that the result depends on the table's sort order and that a prefix chain can be missed; stated.

name: ref_findmust
prose: Precondition: p and g are valid; g->strip is an SOP program ending in OEND; g->must is NULL and g->mlen is 0 from setup. Postcondition: returns nothing. If p->error != 0 it returns at once without touching g. If MB_CUR_MAX > 1 and the current locale encoding is not UTF-8 it also returns without touching g. Otherwise it sets g->moffset = 0 and scans the program for the longest run of OCHAR operators (counting bytes of their multibyte encoding, first-found wins on ties), tracking an offset; if skipping an OQUEST_/OCH_ group finds an operator that is not O_QUEST, O_CH or OOR2 it sets BAD in g->iflags and returns (g->mlen and g->moffset may already have been updated). After the scan, if g->mlen == 0 it sets g->moffset = -1 and returns. Otherwise it mallocs g->mlen + 1 bytes; if malloc fails it sets g->must = NULL (the malloc result), g->mlen = 0, g->moffset = -1 and returns. Otherwise g->must holds the NUL-terminated byte string of the longest run and g->mlen its length, and g->moffset is the computed offset (which can be -1 when it could not be determined).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_findmust (oracle.c:1847-2015). Reviewer round 15 is right: line 1997-2001 assigns g->must from malloc, so it becomes NULL on failure, not 'unchanged'. Note g->moffset is set to 0 at line 1876 right after the two early returns.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: calls build_pool(), runs the hand-written run_case pairs, then every ordered pair of the NPOOL pool patterns, then seeds rng_state with a fixed constant and runs 260000 randomised run_case calls; prints a header, one row per function (name, cases, failures) and a line 'PASS' or 'FAIL' followed by the failure total; returns 0 if the total failure count is zero and 1 otherwise.
note: slice shows the tail of main (harness.cpp:232-365). Contract removed because main drives global state.

name: float32_lt
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: static function. If either operand is a NaN (exponent field 0xFF and non-zero fraction, quiet or signalling), it calls float_raise(float_flag_invalid), which ORs 16 into the global ref_float_exception_flags, and returns 0. Otherwise it returns 1 exactly when a < b as IEEE values: if the signs differ it returns 1 when a is negative and not both operands are zero (so -0 and +0 give 0), else 0; if the signs match it returns 1 when a != b and (for positive operands) a < b as bit patterns or (for negative operands) a > b as bit patterns. The only memory it modifies is ref_float_exception_flags (and only in the NaN case).
note: checked oracle.c:55-71. Contract emptied: it touched a global (exception flags), and reviewer round 15 is right that the old contract omitted that side effect.

name: ref_float32_lt
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: returns float32_lt(a, b) unchanged: 1 exactly when neither operand is a NaN and a < b (so -0 and +0 give 0), and 0 otherwise. When either operand is a NaN, float32_lt ORs float_flag_invalid (16) into the global ref_float_exception_flags before returning 0; that is the only memory touched.
note: checked oracle.c:73-78. Contract emptied (global side effect); reviewer round 15 right.

name: ref___ltsf2
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit patterns read as IEEE single-precision values. Postcondition: returns -float32_lt(a, b): -1 exactly when neither operand is a NaN and a < b, and 0 otherwise (including when either operand is a NaN and when a == b or a > b). When either operand is a NaN, float32_lt ORs float_flag_invalid into the global ref_float_exception_flags; that is the only memory touched.
note: checked oracle.c:92-98. Reviewer round 1 (prose reverses return values) was about older wording; current text matches the code. Contract emptied (global side effect).

name: rand_f64
prose: Precondition: prng_state holds any uint64_t value (normally set by prng_seed). Postcondition: draws r = prng_next() and switches on r & 7. Cases 0, 1 and 2 return one further prng_next() value. Case 3 returns sign (bit 8 of r) | 0x7FF0000000000000 | frac, where frac is the low 52 bits of a further draw, reduced with frac &= 0xF (all bits above the low nibble cleared) when (r >> 9) & 3 == 0; this is an infinity or a NaN. Case 4 returns sign | frac with exponent zero, frac being the low 52 bits of a further draw, set to 0 when (r >> 9) & 3 == 0 and masked to its low 8 bits when it equals 1; this is a signed zero or subnormal. Case 5 draws q to pick one of the 11 exponents {0, 1, 2, 0x3FD, 0x3FE, 0x3FF, 0x400, 0x401, 0x7FD, 0x7FE, 0x7FF} (q mod 11) and a further draw for a 52-bit fraction, and returns sign | exponent | fraction. Case 6 draws q and returns the value whose eight bytes are 0x80 | (corresponding byte of q & 0x7F). Case 7 draws q and returns sign | (0x3FF + q % 5 - 2) << 52 with zero fraction. prng_state is advanced by two prng_next calls in every case except case 5, where it advances by three.
note: checked harness.cpp:90-140. Reviewer round 15 is right: frac &= 0xF keeps only the low nibble, the old prose said the opposite. Reviewer round 2 (one further draw in most branches) is consistent with the old 'two calls total'.

name: ref_float32_to_float64
prose: Precondition: none; a is any 32-bit single-precision bit pattern. Postcondition: for an infinity it returns the double infinity with the same sign; for a NaN it returns ref_commonNaNToFloat64(ref_float32ToCommonNaN(a)), a quiet double NaN (0x7FF8... bit set) with a's sign and payload, and raises float_flag_invalid if a is a signalling NaN; for zero it returns a zero of the same sign; for a subnormal it normalises and returns the exactly equal double; for a normal number it returns the exactly equal double (exponent rebiased by 0x380, fraction shifted). No rounding occurs and no flag is raised except invalid for a signalling NaN.
note: checked oracle.c:1732-1753, ref_float32ToCommonNaN (987-997) and ref_commonNaNToFloat64 (1107-1115). Reviewer round 15 right: the common-NaN path raises invalid for a signalling NaN, so 'no flags' was wrong. 'Quiet' is correct because 0x7FF8000000000000 is OR-ed in.

name: ref_addFloat32Sigs
prose: Precondition: a and b are 32-bit single-precision patterns and zSign is 0 or 1; it adds the absolute values, so it is meant to be called with zSign equal to the sign of the intended result. Postcondition: let aExp, bExp be the exponent fields. If aExp > bExp: if aExp is 0xFF it returns ref_propagateFloat32NaN(a, b) when a is a NaN, otherwise a unchanged (its own sign, not zSign). If aExp < bExp: if bExp is 0xFF it returns ref_propagateFloat32NaN(a, b) when b is a NaN, otherwise an infinity with sign zSign. If the exponents are equal: if aExp is 0xFF it returns the NaN from ref_propagateFloat32NaN when either fraction is non-zero, otherwise a unchanged (this includes both operands being infinite); if aExp is 0 it returns the exact sum of the two subnormal fractions packed with sign zSign and exponent field 0 (so a zero result carries sign zSign); otherwise it rounds the sum. In the remaining cases it aligns the smaller operand (shifting with jamming), adds the significands and returns ref_roundAndPackFloat32(zSign, zExp, zSig), i.e. |a| + |b| rounded under the global float_rounding_mode with sign zSign. The called helpers may set bits in the global exception flags.
note: checked oracle.c:1828-1889. Reviewer round 15 is right: when both operands are infinite the result is a, not an infinity with sign zSign; the old prose listed the b-infinite case without excluding a being infinite.

name: ref_float64_to_int32_round_to_zero
prose: Precondition: none; a is any 64-bit double bit pattern. Postcondition: with shiftCount = aExp - 0x413: if |a| < 1 it returns 0, setting float_flag_inexact when a is non-zero (zero gives 0 with no flag). If aExp > 0x41E (|a| >= 2^32, an infinity or a NaN) it raises invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for a NaN or positive a and INT32_MIN for negative a. Otherwise it computes the truncated magnitude absZ (as an unsigned 32-bit value) and z = -absZ for negative a, absZ for positive a; if the sign of z disagrees with the sign of a and z is non-zero it raises invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for positive a, INT32_MIN for negative a. This also covers 2^31 <= a < 2^32. A negative a whose truncated magnitude is exactly 2^31 (that is, -2^31 - 1 < a <= -2^31) returns INT32_MIN without raising invalid (inexact is raised if a has a fractional part). In the non-invalid cases it returns z and sets float_flag_inexact if any discarded bits were non-zero. Invalid is raised through ref_float_raise; the inexact bit is ORed into float_exception_flags.
note: checked oracle.c:2521-2561. Reviewer round 2 and 15 both right: values in (-2^31-1, -2^31] truncate to -2^31 with no invalid.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: calls t_uc for every value 0..UCHAR_MAX and t_us for every value 0..USHRT_MAX, calls build_edges() and t_all on each edge value, then runs 250000 t_all(gen()) cases; prints a header, one row per function (name, cases, failures, PASS or FAIL) and a TOTAL row; returns 0 if the total failure count is zero and 1 otherwise.
note: slice shows the tail of main (harness.cpp:251-287). Contract removed because main drives global statistics.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: if pbsd_shim_init() returns a negative value it writes 'pbsd_shim_init failed' to stderr and returns 1. Otherwise it runs the ten test routines (handwritten and random tempnam, vsnprintf_l, vsnprintf, arginfo_quote, render_quote), prints a header and, for each of the NSTAT entries of g_stat, a row (name, cases, fails) while summing the failures, and returns 0 if the sum is zero and 1 otherwise.
note: the listed name print_stats is not a function; lines 1053-1062 are the tail of main (harness.cpp:1031-1062).

name: ref___printf_render_float
prose: Precondition: io is a valid output stream, pi describes a floating conversion (spec one of a, A, e, E, f, F, g, G; any other spec reaches an assert(pi->spec == 'f')), and arg[0] points to a double, or to a long double when pi->is_long_double is set. Postcondition: it converts the value with __hdtoa/__hldtoa (a, A) or dtoa/__ldtoa (other specs), builds sign, optional 0x prefix, digits, decimal point, locale grouping separators (the grouping table is consulted only when pi->alt is set) and exponent, and writes them to io with padding (blank, zero or left-adjusted according to pi->pad, pi->left and pi->width) through __printf_pad and __printf_puts. Infinity and NaN are printed as 'inf'/'INF' or 'nan'/'NAN' (lower case when spec >= 'a'), with no sign for NaN. After output it calls __printf_flush(io), frees the dtoa buffer with freedtoa if one was allocated, and returns ret, the sum of the values returned by the __printf_pad and __printf_puts calls. It has a single return (line 421).
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref___printf_render_float (oracle.c:148-422); the slice is the second half. Checked all paths via goto fp_common and goto here to the single return.

name: test_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: none; a static void function without parameters that uses its own stack buffers and the helpers case_recvmsg and rng_*. Postcondition: sets up a zeroed msghdr pointing at its name, control and iov buffers; calls case_recvmsg with a NULL msghdr for every combination of 10 socket values, 9 flag values and 9 return values; calls case_recvmsg for each of the 10 socket values with a zero-length msghdr (namelen, iovlen, controllen all 0), flags 0 and ret 0; runs a loop that steps an unsigned char b by 0x3f (8-bit wraparound) from 0 until it reaches 0xff (65 iterations), each time with msg_namelen = 1, msg_iovlen = 1 and one 1-byte iov, passing b as the flags and (int8_t)b as the return value; runs a loop with cnt from 0 to IOV_MAX_TEST + 2, filling the first min(cnt, IOV_MAX_TEST) iovs, with namelen 4, iovlen cnt, controllen MSG_CTRL_CAP, socket 7, flags cnt and ret cnt; and finally seeds the generator with 0x7263766d and runs 200000 random cases with random sizes for name, control and iov data. It returns void and leaves nothing allocated.
note: checked harness.cpp:755-844. Reviewer round 15 is right: the byte sweep is over flags/return value with namelen and iovlen fixed at 1; the namelen and iovlen sweeps are in the cnt loop and the random loop. The 65-iteration count is from a quick simulation of the unsigned-char loop.

name: ref__Tthr_kill
prose: Precondition: pthread is a thread handle, sig a signal number; _get_curthread, _thr_find_thread, _thr_send_sig and THR_THREAD_UNLOCK are test doubles in this oracle (a real implementation would lock the target in _thr_find_thread). Postcondition: if sig < 0 or sig > _SIG_MAXSIG it returns EINVAL and does nothing else. Otherwise it takes curthread = _get_curthread(). If curthread == pthread it calls _thr_send_sig(pthread, sig) only when sig > 0 and returns 0. Otherwise it calls _thr_find_thread(curthread, pthread, 0); if that returns 0 it calls _thr_send_sig only when sig > 0 and then THR_THREAD_UNLOCK(curthread, pthread), and returns 0; if it returns a non-zero value it returns that value with no signal sent and no unlock call.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref__Tthr_kill (oracle.c:497-527), not pthread_kill. The old prose omitted the EINVAL return for an out-of-range signal (lines 503-505).

name: DEFINE_UNARY_CASE(__kernel_cospil, st_kcospil)
prose: Generated function case___kernel_cospil(long double x) (static void), produced by the DEFINE_UNARY_CASE macro (harness.cpp:387-401). Precondition: none; st_kcospil is the file-scope Stat. Postcondition: increments st_kcospil.cases, computes p = port::__kernel_cospil(x) and r = ref___kernel_cospil(x); if same_ld(p, r) is false it calls fail_head(st_kcospil), which always increments st_kcospil.fails and returns true only while fewer than MAX_SHOWN (6) failures have been shown (it then prints 'FAIL <name>: '); in that case it also prints x, the port value and the ref value and a newline. Nothing is returned.
note: checked harness.cpp:105-114 and 387-403. Old prose said a diagnostic is printed 'iff results differ and fail_head permits' but did not say that the failure counter is bumped on every difference.

name: cexpl
prose: Precondition: z is any long double complex value passed by value. Postcondition: with x = creall(z) and y = cimagl(z), the first matching case applies, in this order: (1) y == 0: returns (expl(x), y). (2) x == 0 (and y != 0): returns (cos y, sin y) from sincosl, for any y including infinities and NaN. (3) y not finite (and x != 0): if x is finite or NaN returns (y - y, y - y), a NaN pair; if x is negative infinity returns (0.0, 0.0); otherwise (x positive infinity) returns (x, y - y). (4) y finite and x != 0: if exp_ovfl < x < cexp_ovfl returns __ldexp_cexpl(z, 0); otherwise (x <= exp_ovfl, x >= cexp_ovfl, or x NaN) returns (expl(x) * cos y, expl(x) * sin y), the cases covering ordinary x, large x and x = +-Inf; a NaN x gives NaN parts. No locks or memory are involved; floating-point exceptions may be raised by the calls.
note: slice cut the head: real function is cexpl (oracle.c:1018-1066). Reviewer round 15 is right: for x == 0 with non-finite y the code returns sincosl(y) (line 1030-1032), not NaN,NaN, because the x == 0 test precedes the isfinite(y) test.

name: tanpil
prose: Precondition: none; x is any long double. Postcondition: with ax = |x|: if ax < 1: for ax < 2^-60 it returns x when x == 0 (signed zero preserved) and otherwise an approximation of pi*x computed with the pi_hi/pi_lo split and rescaled by 2^-113; for 2^-60 <= ax < 0.5 it uses t = __kernel_tanpil(ax); for ax == 0.5 it uses t = 1/vzero (positive infinity); for 0.5 < ax < 1 it uses t = -__kernel_tanpil(1 - ax); in these three cases it returns -t if x < 0 and t otherwise. If 1 <= ax < 2^112 it splits ax into integer part ai and fraction ar with FFLOORL128, sets odd = +1 when ai is even and -1 when odd, and uses t = copysign(0, odd) when ar == 0 (zero whose sign depends on the parity of ai), __kernel_tanpil(ar) for 0 < ar < 0.5, odd/vzero (an infinity whose sign depends on the parity) for ar == 0.5, and -__kernel_tanpil(1 - ar) for ar > 0.5; it returns -t if x < 0 and t otherwise. If x is an infinity or NaN it returns vzero/vzero (NaN). For finite ax >= 2^112 it returns zero with the sign of x (copysignl of t, x). It has no side effects other than floating-point exceptions.
note: slice cut the head: real function is tanpil (oracle.c:231-283). Reviewer round 15 is right: the sign of the zero for integer ax in [1, 2^112) depends on the parity of the integer part, not only on the sign of x. For ax >= 2^112 the result takes the sign of x (line 282), so parity does not matter there.

name: ref_powl
prose: Precondition: x and y are long double values. Postcondition: this slice holds only the tail of ref_powl (x raised to y). The function returns, in order of checks: 1 if y is zero; 1 if x == 1 or if x == -1 and y is infinite; the NaN from nan_mix(x, y) if either operand is a NaN; for y = +-infinity, y - y (NaN) for |x| == 1, y or 0 for |x| > 1 and -y or 0 for |x| < 1; 1/x if y is -1 and x if y is +1, x*x for y == 2, sqrtl(x) for y == 0.5 and x >= +0; for x equal to +-0, +-infinity or +-1 it returns |x| (or 1/|x| when y < 0) with its sign negated when x < 0 and y is an odd integer, or NaN when x is -1 and y is not an integer; NaN for x < 0 and y not an integer; overflow (huge*huge) or underflow (tiny*tiny) for very large |y| unless x is close to 1. Otherwise (the part in the slice) it computes log2|x| in extended precision, forms z = y*log2|x|, and returns s*huge*huge (overflow) when z > 16384 (or z == 16384 and p_l + ovt > z - p_h), s*tiny*tiny (underflow) when z < -16495 (or z == -16495 and p_l <= z - p_h), and otherwise s*2^z computed by reducing z (n = nearest integer, polynomial for 2^(z-n), exponent adjusted by n, via scalbnl when the result is subnormal), where s is -1 when x < 0 and y is an odd integer and +1 otherwise.
note: slice cut the head and the name was wrong: the listed 'expl' is the tail of ref_powl (oracle.c:288-583); the slice also contains the start of the exp2l section (line 606+) but no expl. Reviewer round 15 is right (s is not the sign of x, thresholds are about z = y*log2|x| rather than exact).

name: ref___kernel_cosl
prose: Precondition: x and y are long double values (the kernel argument and its tail). Postcondition: returns a long double computed as z = x*x, r = z*(C1 + z*(C2 + z*(C3 + z*(C4 + z*(C5 + z*(C6 + z*C7)))))), hz = 0.5*z, w = 1 - hz, and w + (((1 - w) - hz) + (z*r - x*y)). On amd64 and i386 C1 is built as (long double)C1hi + C1lo from two doubles. It reads constants and modifies no memory.
note: slice cut the head: the function is ref___kernel_cosl on long double arguments (oracle.c:247-257), not a double __kernel_cos; the old prose described double arguments and a polynomial without the outer z factor. I kept the statement to the arithmetic in the body and made no accuracy claim.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: runs the edge, walk, bit-pattern and random (210000 iterations) check_* cases, which update the stats of scalbnf, fabsf, copysign and gammaf; prints a header, one row per stat (name, cases, failures) and a TOTAL row; sets a failure flag if any of the four stats has zero cases (printing '<name>: no cases were run') or a non-zero failure count; prints 'FAIL' or 'PASS' and returns 1 if the flag is set and 0 otherwise.
note: the listed 'unnamed test-summary function' is the tail of main (harness.cpp:409-548). Old prose ('all[0..nall-1] valid records') described only the end of main.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (main takes no arguments). Postcondition: main runs the whole lrint, fmax, fmin and fminimum_magl test program (edge vectors under rounding modes, cross products, signed zero, branch and bit tests, NaN boundaries, and RANDOM_ITERS random cases) and so updates the stats st_lrint, st_fmax, st_fmin and st_fminimum_magl; it then prints a per-function table and a TOTAL row, sets a failure flag if any of the four stats has zero cases (printing '<name>: no cases were run') or a non-zero failure count, prints 'FAIL' or 'PASS' and returns 1 if the flag is set and 0 otherwise.

name: __kernel_rem_pio2
prose: Precondition: x points to nx doubles holding successive 24-bit integer pieces of a positive value whose scaled exponent is e0 (e0 <= 16360); prec is 0 (single), 1 (double), 2 (extended) or 3 (quad); y has room for 1 element when prec == 0, 2 when prec is 1 or 2, and 3 when prec == 3; nx and the derived jk keep the 20-element local arrays in range. Postcondition: reduces the value modulo pi/2 using the table ipio2 and writes the reduced argument to y: y[0] for prec 0; y[0] and y[1] for prec 1 or 2; y[0], y[1] and y[2] for prec 3, each negated when the internal flag ih is non-zero. It returns n & 7, the low three bits of the quotient (octant). It may recompute with more terms of ipio2 until the result is non-zero, and it modifies no memory other than y and its locals.
note: slice cut the head: real function is __kernel_rem_pio2 (oracle.c:431-580). Reviewer round 15 is right: y is not filled for 0..prec, only 1, 2 or 3 elements are written (lines 549, 556-559, 574-577). Old prose said prec+1 elements; that is wrong for prec 2 and 3.

name: ref_acosh
prose: Precondition: none; any double x. Postcondition: using the high word hx of x: if hx < 0x3ff00000 (x below 1, which includes every negative value, -0, -infinity and negative NaNs because hx is signed) it returns (x - x)/(x - x), a NaN. If hx >= 0x41b00000 (|x| >= 2^28): for hx >= 0x7ff00000 (+infinity or positive NaN) it returns x + x, otherwise log(x) + ln2. Else if x == 1.0 exactly it returns 0.0. Else if hx > 0x40000000 (x of about 2 or above, up to 2^28) it returns log(2x - 1/(x + sqrt(x*x - 1))). Otherwise (1 < x with high word at most 0x40000000, which includes x just above 2 up to the next high-word step) it sets t = x - 1 and returns log1p(t + sqrt(2t + t*t)). No state is modified.
note: checked oracle.c:38-60. Reviewer round 2 right (negative NaN takes the x<1 branch); round 15 right (the log1p formula is used until the high word exceeds 0x40000000, i.e. slightly beyond x = 2); round 1 right about the huge branch.
